findings.title: isinstance guard prevents killing spawn-context flusher processes
findings.body: In `_ensure_processes_alive` the call `process.kill()` is now guarded by `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)`. On Linux, `multiprocessing.Process` resolves to the default (fork) class `ForkProcess`, while these flusher workers are created with `multiprocessing.get_context("spawn").Process`, i.e. `SpawnProcess`. `SpawnProcess` is a sibling of `ForkProcess` (both subclass `BaseProcess`), not a subclass of it, so this check is False and `kill()` never runs. As a result a dead or hung worker is never terminated before a replacement is spawned: dead children become zombies (never reaped) and hung children keep running and flushing the same shards concurrently with the new worker, leading to duplicate/partial writes to `buffered-segments`. The pre-PR code called `self.process.kill()` unconditionally (with a `ValueError` catch), so this is a regression. The same guard at line 346 also means `terminate()` in `join()` never fires for spawn processes. Use `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.process.BaseProcess)` or `not isinstance(process, threading.Thread)` (and keep the added `AttributeError` guard for the thread case).

findings.title: join() skips waiting for and terminating remaining workers once the shared deadline is reached
findings.body: `join()` iterates the worker processes and does `break` whenever `deadline - time.time() <= 0`. If the timeout is exhausted while waiting on an earlier worker (or already consumed by `next_step.join(timeout)`), all remaining workers are neither waited on nor terminated, so shutdown returns while they are still running and producing to Kafka. The previous single-process implementation always executed `terminate()` after the wait loop regardless of whether the deadline had passed. With multiple workers this needs to attempt termination of every worker even after the deadline, otherwise a hung worker keeps flushing after a rebalance/shutdown.

findings.title: Added time.sleep(0.1) is a no-op because time.sleep is monkeypatched
findings.body: The test sets `monkeypatch.setattr("time.sleep", lambda _: None)` at line 14, which patches the global `time.sleep`, so the newly added `time.sleep(0.1)` on line 62 does nothing and the comment 'Give flusher threads time to process after drift change' is false. `step.poll()` also does not drive the flusher's background loop (SpanFlusher.poll only polls `next_step`). Nothing therefore guarantees the flusher thread completes a `flush_segments` iteration after `current_drift` is set and before `step.join()` sets `stopped`, so the test races with thread scheduling and can be flaky. Use a real sleep (e.g. only patch the flusher's sleep) or synchronize deterministically on an event/message.

findings.title: New test only exercises the thread path and does not cover the real multiprocessing behavior
findings.body: `test_flusher_processes_limit` passes `produce_to_pipe`, which makes `SpanFlusher` use `threading.Thread` instead of spawn processes. The actual production path (`mp_context.Process`, pickling the per-shard buffer, `kill`/`terminate`, worker restart) is never exercised, and the assertions only check process count and the trivial sum of shard-list lengths. Consequently the spawn-process bugs in this PR (e.g. the `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)` kill/terminate issue) are invisible to CI. Add coverage that uses spawn processes and/or verifies the restart path and that each process actually flushes its assigned shards.

findings.title: Shard metric tag uses inconsistent key and a comma-joined shard list as its value
findings.body: The produce timer uses tag key `shard` (line 185) while the wait_produce timer uses `shards` (line 199), and both pass `shard_tag` — the comma-joined list of all shards owned by the process (e.g. `"0,1,2,3"`) — as the value. This mislabels the metric (the value is a combination of shards, not a single shard), makes the tag cardinality the set of distinct shard groupings, and the differing key means dashboards/alerts querying `shard` versus `shards` will not line up. Use one consistent key and emit one data point per shard, or a fixed process-index tag.

findings.title: `_create_process_for_shard` is dead code
findings.body: `_create_process_for_shard(self, shard)` is never called; restarts are performed by `_ensure_processes_alive` via `_create_process_for_shards(process_index, shards)`. The unused helper is dead code and suggests an intended per-shard restart API that was never wired up. Remove it or use it.

findings.title: Class docstring claims one process per shard, but shards are shared across at most max_processes workers
findings.body: The docstring now says 'Creates one process per shard for parallel processing', but the implementation computes `num_processes = min(max_processes, len(assigned_shards))` and distributes shards round-robin across that many processes, so each process may own several shards (and fewer processes than shards are run when the limit applies). The docstring should describe 'up to max_processes workers, each handling a subset of shards' so the documented behavior matches the code.
